1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.
LAC no. 322/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Narayan Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 2.

sentences.text:
The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 4//7 (416), 8/2(20), 28//1(416), 10/1 (38), 22//25/1(05), 23//6/1(28), 7/1(28)
i.e. total area measuring 19 LAC no. 322/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Narayan Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 Bigha and 16 Biswas, having 1/2th share each, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).

sentences.text:
5. It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
6.

Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :
i) The LAC has not adopted correct method of assessment of market value of the said land on imaginary basis and on the basis of a government police.
The market value of the acquired land is only to be assessed and determined strictly as provided by law U/s 23 and 24 of LA Act, 1894.

sentences.text: The LAC has not considered the location, developments, existing utility and potentiality of the land.
The present physical and existing location, developments and the utility and potentiality of the land, in and around the land of the petitioners were not taken into account.
iii) The LAC has erred in not taking into consideration the future potentiality and the utility of the acquired land of the petitioners.

The impugned award is arbitrary,
malafide and detrimental to the interest of the petitioners i.e. farmers.

The land of the petitioners has an increasing trend as regard to the market value after fixation of the rates of the agricultural land in Delhi and such rates have been increased by more than ten times.

LAC no. 322/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Narayan Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 The land of the petitioners have a very high value and is very fertile and leveled without any kind of depression or defect.

sentences.text: The said land be used for industrial or commercial or residential use with little efforts.
iv) The land of the petitioners is adjacent to welldeveloped areas, colonies and village Abadi and hence has a great market value.

The land enjoys all type of facilities/ civic amenities like developed metalled roads, electricity, hospitals, government schools, public schools, computer institutes, full fledged post office, health gym, modern panchayat ghar, and most frequently served by DTC and various other private transporters as GT Road i.e. NH10, DelhiFirozpur Railway Line and main DelhiKanjhawala road passes by the side of village Mubarakpur Dabas.
There are nationalised bank operating with well established hospital and fully developed markets in village Mubarakpur Dabas.
Land is also surrounded by Ghevara Industrial Area, Savada Industrial Area, Mundka Industrial Area with several godowns which are adjacent to the said village.

Government has provided all civic amenities like roads, transportation, electricity, water connections, schools,
hospitals, telecommunications, etc where the market value is more than Rs. 10,000/ per sq. yards.
Therefore, the price of the acquired land should have been assessed minimum @ Rs 10,000/ per sq. yards.
v) The LAC has not taken into consideration the relevant sale/purchase transactions of the land in village Mubarakpur Dabas and in the adjoining villages itself.

LAC has not announced any compensation for he standing crop of the petitioners and besides this, the petitioner were fully LAC no. 322/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Narayan Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 dependent upon their agricultural land which has been acquired and not the petitioners are left without any source of income.

Further,
an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/ should be granted to the petitioners for damages and substantial loss suffered as a result of severance of their leftover land.
vi) The LAC has not considered the increase of 15 % per annum in the value of the land between the date of notification and the date of announcement of the Award.

It is alleged that the LAC further has assessed the compensation merely on the basis of surmises and conjuctures and without looking Narayan Singh (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103431094/

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 i.e. Union of India and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the said land was acquired for the purpose of PDD, therefore, DDA is a necessary and proper party for complete adjudication of the present reference petition.
The present reference petition U/s 18 of LA Act is time barred therefore, the reference is dismissed on the point of limitation.
Further, the land in question is not surrounded by any developed or underdeveloped colony and can only be used for agriculture.
There were no structures, trees, well or tube well on the land in question at the time of publication of notification U/s 4 of LA Act.
The petitioner is also not entitled for any enhancement in the compensation since they have not filed their claim in response to notices under Section 9 and 10 of LA Act.
The land is also disputed with the Gaon Sabha of the said village.
The petitioner is not entitled to get any interest on the amount till the case is adjourned sinedie.
All the other averments made in the reference petition were strictly denied and opposed and is liable to be dismissed.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner is entitled to the enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
15. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.

Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned Narayan Singh (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103431094/
5 case.
17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

18. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been LAC no. 322/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Narayan Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

entities.text: Narayan Singh Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 21.

As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No. 28//1 (416), 10/1(308), 22//25/1(005) 23//6/1 (2 LAC no. 322/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Narayan Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 08), 7/1 (208), has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.

22. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.
(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2)
 of the Act).
